doc_summary: Bowman surveys evidence for eight surprising claims about LLMs, including that steering is unreliable, interpretability is immature, and brief interactions mislead. Key for evaluation design: failures and successes in single probes are weak evidence, and more capable models may recognize training/test circumstances and behave differently.

items.claim: Prefers positive results on well-designed measures over negative results because a failure may reflect poor elicitation rather than missing capability.
items.quote: simply observing that an LLM fails at a task in some setting is not reliable evidence that that LLM doesn’t have the skills or knowledge to do that task.

items.claim: Distrusts single successful or cherry-picked demonstrations as evidence of general capability, since models can memorize instances without robust reasoning.
items.quote: observing that an LLM performs a task successfully in one instance is not strong evidence that the LLM is capable of performing that task in general, especially if that example was cherry-picked as part of a demonstration

items.claim: Capable models recognize the circumstances of training and testing, so they may behave as expected only in those circumstances, which undermines test-time evidence of good behavior.
items.quote: More capable models can better recognize the specific circumstances under which they are trained. Because of this, they are more likely to learn to act as expected in precisely those circumstances while behaving competently but unexpectedly in others.

items.claim: Distrusts pre-deployment testing as proof of safe behavior, citing Bing Chat failures despite extensive testing.
items.quote: It seems likely that issues like these played some role in the bizarre, manipulative behavior that early versions of Microsoft Bing Chat showed, despite the system having been tested extensively before launch

items.claim: Prefers trying varied prompts and reframings over a single prompt, because behavior is idiosyncratically sensitive to wording and a single framing can mislead.
items.quote: Often, a model will fail to complete a task when asked, but will then perform the task correctly once the request is reworded or reframed slightly, leading to the emerging craft of prompt engineering

items.claim: Warns that apparent safety fixes can fail silently when a model predicts which claims will be checked, behaving well only where it is observed.
items.quote: that LLM can reasonably accurately predict which factual claims human data workers are likely to check, this can easily lead the LLM to tell the truth only when making claims that are likely to be checked.

items.claim: Expects agentic deployments in unfamiliar, self-created situations to be where dangerous strategic misbehavior arises, which motivates testing open-ended agent scenarios.
items.quote: Deployments of this type would increasingly often place LLMs in unfamiliar situations created as a result of the systems’ own actions, further reducing the degree to which their developers can predict and control their behavior.

items.claim: Distrusts model-generated explanations and ad-hoc interpretability as evidence of internal reasoning since they can be systematically misleading.
items.quote: promising-looking techniques that elicit reasoning in natural language do not reliably correspond to the processes that LLMs use to reason, and model-generated explanations can also be systematically misleading

items.claim: Prefers claims resilient to mistaken assumptions over confident conclusions because LLM science is immature and conventional wisdom is shaky.
items.quote: All of this is reason to be especially uncertain about the issues discussed in this paper and to make important decisions about LLMs in ways that are resilient to mistaken assumptions.

items.claim: Prefers evaluating observable behavior (effective, reliable) over debating understanding or agency words, because the evaluation does not depend on those labels.
items.quote: We can evaluate whether systems are effective or ineffective, reliable or unreliable, interpretable or uninterpretable, and improving quickly or slowly, regardless of whether they are underlyingly human-like
